rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **Electric potential** is work per unit positive charge brought from infinity: $V = W/q$, in volts (1 V = 1 J/C — NEB 2023 MCQ). The **potential difference** moves charge between points: $W = qV$, or $W = neV$ for n electrons (NEB 2022, 4m). A point charge gives $V = kq/r$ — a **scalar** — so 2 μC at 0.5 m produces 36 kV (NEB 2024, 2m).…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - V = W/q; 1 V = 1 J/C - V_point = kq/r; U = kq₁q₂/r - 1 eV = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ J; W = neV (n electrons)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Potential is a scalar:** add kq/r values with signs, no directions needed.  ·  **E goes as 1/r²; V goes as 1/r** — don't mix the two formulas.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: A sketched sign convention is part of the data.  ·  A dimensionless ratio still needs the two quantities named.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***NEB 2024*** — V at 0.5 m from 2 μC = 36 kV; U of ± pair = −0.18 J.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Covers only: potential difference, potential due to a point charge, potential energy, electron volt (within Potential, Potential Difference and Potential Energy).  ·  Out of scope here: topics of neighbouring units in Physics — don't mix them.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Copy the worked example and hide the result until the last step.  ·  Name the unit of every term in the formula.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: "eV = qV/1.6×10⁻¹⁹ — and remember V is scalar."

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **Numerical (3m): Find U for charges +5 μC and +2 μC at 0.1 m.** — U = 9×10⁹ × 10⁻¹¹/0.1 = 9×10⁻² J = 0.09 J (positive — like charges cost work to assemble).

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: Quote the sign of U — negative means bound.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: **W = qV is the workhorse** — every electron-volt and battery calculation starts here.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: V = W/q (volt = J/C); V_point = kq/r; U = kq₁q₂/r; 1 eV = 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ J.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: A 1.5 V battery gives each coulomb 1.5 J of energy — the same potential language powers homes and atoms.

rows.label: MCQ drill
rows.text: Potential is → B  ·  Potential energy of charge q is → A

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Energy Landscape of Charge Electric potential is electrostatics' energy language: instead of asking how strongly a charge is pushed, we ask how much work it takes to move it. Volts, electron-volts and the kq/r formula make field problems as easy as bookkeeping.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts (NEB 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024) ### 2.1 Potential and potential difference - **Electric potential at a point:** the work done per unit positive charge in bringing it from infinity to that point without acceleration: $$V = \frac{W}{q} \qquad \text{SI unit: volt (V) = J C}^{-1}$$ - **Potential difference** between two points: work per unit charge…  ·  ## 3. Conceptual Relationships - **To Topic 87:** V is the line integral of E; E is the gradient of V. - **To Topic 91:** equipotential surfaces are V = constant maps. - **To capacitors (Unit 24):** U = ½CV² stores energy in the same language.
